review_scope: Round-018 independent hostile validation of the CURRENT Android MCP bridge DESIGN only. Inputs: 'design-c4/docs/Android MCP Bridge Design.md' (206076 bytes, four slices 0-55000/55000-110000/110000-165000/165000-206076), architecture/workspace.dsl and architecture/code-diagrams.md (verbatim), architecture/round013-design-corrections.md (verbatim excerpt), 16 Structurizr/PlantUML diagram SVGs, 13 screen/storyboard SVGs, build.gradle.kts and Gradle pins, storyboards/storyboard.md, ui docs and ui-asset-manifest.json, finding-ledger-design014.json, current-design-archive-validation.json, catalog/SOURCE-METADATA-CONTRACT.md (supporting contract, CRUD semantics only), six build receipts, pinned remote_control.proto. Excluded from scoring: Google API inventory completeness, source acquisition, parser/extractor correctness, catalog population, unmatched annotation counts, native-source completeness, deployment. The original failed core pass contributes nothing; its bytes are covered by core-section 1-4 plus the two verbatim reconciliation excerpts.
verdict: NOT_ACCEPTED at the requested 98/98 design bar. The design is architecturally coherent, consistently distinguishes plans from proven implementation, and its platform and protocol claims are mostly correct and honestly bounded. It nevertheless carries 3 high and 17 medium concrete contradictions or unspecified mechanisms (F-01..F-20) that change behavior or understanding, plus five grouped low residual sets (F-21..F-25). No finding depends on dataset or app completeness.

design.rationale: Accuracy deductions come from internal contradictions, not from false platform claims: superseded ARC/UI positions remain normative in four sections (F-04); a schema admits an executor backend that the forwarding rules make impossible (F-02); the callback_descriptors CHECK forces false materialization claims (F-03); 'pinned plan' versus 'rejected with stale_contract' (F-08); container/deployment labels misstate the APK's interactions and the CallbackFlow view is consistent with a forbidden protocol reading (F-01, F-12, F-13); the same class carries disjoint contracts across code views and the design-doc class table uses a different vocabulary (F-11); two reason-code grammars (F-14); 'or'-joined delete semantics and a credential-kind rule that contradicts its own separation claim (F-15); an ARC identifier of unverified provenance presented as what existing clients use (F-18). Completeness deductions: no model path for tools/call dispatch, resources/subscribe/read, cancel and cleanup (F-01); concrete-class callbacks unclassified (F-03); subscription transition table for death/lease/timeout absent (F-07); health tuple and AppBar status element never specified once (F-09); paired-ADB ownership, client realization and deployment topology (F-10); pairing message sequence and TLS host candidate (F-06); negotiated direct stream is a placeholder (F-17); envelope 1.0 vs package 0.8.0 absent from inspected text (F-18); storyboards cover three of the required flow families with placeholder panels (F-19); canonicalization unpinned for cross-language hashes (F-16); toolchain pins incomplete for the determinism claim (F-20). Credits: every requirement has a specified mechanism in prose except the direct stream; protected-owner authentication, pairing proof, Binder acquisition routes, backpressure, startup reuse, lease renewal, admin-route gating, brightness range, MCP resource/journal semantics and ARC framing facts were verified consistent across independent slices and the pinned proto. Scores are not averaged across workpapers; each is a single judgment of the whole design.

findings.area: C4 model and code views: MCP request/read paths (req 7, 9, 10)
findings.artifact: architecture/workspace.dsl (model relationships, dynamic CallbackFlow); architecture/code-diagrams.md blocks server-core-classes and server-execution-classes; docs/diagrams/structurizr-CallbackFlow.svg, structurizr-ExecutionComponents.svg, server-core-classes.svg, server-execution-classes.svg
findings.issue: At component, dynamic and class level the model cannot trace tools/call dispatch, resources/subscribe, resources/read of finite journal pages, callback.cancel, or execution of the recorded cleanup/unregister plan against the OS; the single read-related edge points from broker to server. The dynamic view as drawn omits the final JSON-RPC response and the subscribe step, which is consistent with the forbidden reading that the POST stream stays open to carry callback updates. The prose (callback section, round013 callback.status/cancel contracts, events_uri status document) specifies these paths, so this is a model accuracy and completeness defect, not a missing mechanism.

findings.area: ADB backend model and remote-host loopback forwarding (req 3, 9)
findings.artifact: Design.md S3 'Endpoint protections'; S15 'Three distinct backend modes', 'SQLite connection and target profiles', 'External host forwarding'; S16 tool table
findings.issue: adb forward carries only host-to-phone connections, and the two channels that could let the phone reach a host adb server (adb reverse, exposing 5037) are prohibited, so the phone-resident bridge has no execution path through a remote host. A connection profile with backend_kind=external_adb is therefore not executable for screen.state/input.tap, yet nothing ties executor_kind=adb to backend_kind=self_adb; the mode is listed as a backend while its description is ingress only. Separately, a client arriving through adb forward presents the host-side Host header (127.0.0.1:<host port>), which fails an exact match against the bound endpoint whenever ports differ; S3 defines no loopback-literal acceptance rule and 'automatic remote tunneling' can be read as excluding the required mode.

findings.issue: (a) Rows with role proven_non_callback or unknown must still carry one of four registrable/abstract-class strategies, so the schema stores a false materialization claim for every non-callback and unknown candidate. (b) Concrete non-final callback classes with overridable no-op methods (reviewer examples: ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback, WebViewClient) require subclassing exactly as abstract classes do, but no value or reason code covers them; the only available labels are factually wrong for them, so requirement 7's 'ALL callback roles' classification is incomplete.

Brightness: 'between 1 (minimum) and 255 (maximum)' with [S15], raw reads reported with a documented-range flag, 16..240 as a separate default write policy; consistent across S12, the permission section, round013 and the ledger, and with the supplied primary fact.

Req 2: all-Kotlin server and Compose UI stated with no .NET runtime; BridgeService owns transport, policy, SQLite, resolution, backends and callbacks; unexported local facade with no SQL or reflection; START_STICKY with null-Intent handling, stopWithTask disabled, desired_state separate from observed health; honest Android 13+ notification denial and boot-restriction statements; admin route disabled by default with a bounded 10-minute owner window; 'No admin route is active merely because this design contains its specification'.

Req 3: generic ADB screen/tap control requires no instrumentation in targets; loopback-only listeners and host forwards with explicit serial and --no-rebind; adb forward not reverse; no 0.0.0.0, 5037 exposure, tcpip 5555 or Internet tunnel.

Req 4: signed 4-byte big-endian length with 8 MiB default max, Bearer in envelope field 4, one request per connection with repeated responses and end_of_stream terminal flag, Cancel(8) declared unsupported with socket-close cancellation, no fake TLS or IsAdbTunnel, OK envelope may carry CommandResult.succeeded=false, FPS parsed not enforced, mouse/wheel/key/text with no multitouch and Avalonia key names, stable/stale node generation with pressed-state release, protected approval/grant screens excluded, pinned commit 19792a52a13a3df342f90bab6b246b547e673919; golden fixtures, bidirectional interoperability and the license-notice gate are labeled plans with no implementation claim. The pinned proto independently confirms authorization field 4, end_of_stream field 6, BRIDGE_METHOD_CANCEL=8, BridgeStatus UNSUPPORTED=5, CommandResult.succeeded, single-pointer input and no handshake message.

Req 5: immutable imports, local overlays, CAS with append-only entry_history_reasons in the same transaction, PUT/DELETE without PATCH, idempotent import and publish, declared permission metadata (RequiresPermission allOf/anyOf/conditional, AIDL EnforcePermission) kept distinct from runtime OS authority and per-client grant; 'an Android annotation never grants a client access'; generated, generic and known-raw paths converge on one canonical binding policy key; discovery and activation cannot grant.

Req 6: platform major/minor via SDK_INT_FULL, extension levels, build/OEM, module and stable-AIDL interface version/hash observed separately; unknown retained, never zero or false; three-state applicability with point evidence (platform_point:[37,2], PLATFORM_APPLICABILITY_UNPROVEN); coherent type closure with graph_digest and schema_hash; atomic sealed activation with generation/epoch CAS and inventory_sha256 membership pins; invalidation on device, backend and catalog changes; 'Declaration order never proves a Binder transaction code'; no universal private access.

Req 7: synchronous replies local, typed, deadline-bounded or unsupported_synchronous_reply; finite subscription descriptor; event envelope with identity, correlation, sequence (decimal string), time, payload and error; journal baseline via resources/read status document plus cursor pages; overflow default closes delivery with buffer_overflow; disk-full marks durability_failed; at-least-once and acceptance-order semantics stated honestly; restart marks OS registrations orphaned; Ask consumed once per registration scope and lease.

Req 8: nine-tool portable bootstrap (android.groups.discover/describe/set_active, binding.invoke, callback.status, callback.cancel, bindings.search/list/get); whole-set CAS activation; deterministic index with optional non-authoritative semantic ranking; bounded summaries and byte/token budgets; unassigned inventory searchable; dynamic aliases opt-in via negotiated extension.

Req 9: POST SSE yields one final JSON-RPC response then terminates; standard notifications on GET SSE/stdio; resources/subscribe exact URI; resources/updated URI only; bounded finite reads; Last-Event-ID distinct from the journal cursor; progress ends with the request; no invented standard method; tools.listChanged advertised only when emitted; no host-context eviction promise; the four cited specification URLs equal the supplied primary facts; disconnection is not cancellation.

Req 10: Structurizr DSL with context, container, four component, four dynamic and one deployment view plus five image views attached to components; code-level detail delivered as inline PlantUML with `!pragma layout smetana` and explicitly labeled 'proposed Kotlin classes/interfaces, not implemented Android code'; no Mermaid or Pele in any current artifact; the DSL parses by inspection with every dynamic step mapped to a declared relationship.

Req 11: Gradle 8.14.3 wrapper pinned with sha256 and validateDistributionUrl; `plugins { base }` resolves no dependencies; tasks validateArchitecture, generateArchitectureDiagrams, generateUiAssets, renderStoryboards, verifyDesignDocs and packageDesignDocs exist; PlantUML jar checksum verified with explicit failure; reproducible zip; SVGs checked for vector text with no raster or script; expected native (11) and code (5) view names match the 16 diagram files.

Req 12: ten screen SVGs and three storyboards are text-based vector files with titles and states covering empty, denied, disconnected and error cases and a protected owner flow; storyboards are explicitly 'not UML message sequences'; relative links resolve within the manifest; honest 'not a running application' labeling; canonical Markdown hash b80baa6c... matches the archive record (206076 bytes).

Honesty of claims: proposed unmeasured p95 targets, the disclaimed Python 4.30 GiB/565.6 s probe, 'explicit protocol design, not an implemented cryptographic handshake claim', 'Existing full-project98/98 acceptance remains unmet', receipts stating actual_app_implemented=false, and ArcEngine labeled 'not implemented' are consistent throughout.

coverage.requirements_covered: All twelve requirements were exercised; requirement 1 was assessed as a mechanism only (inventory retention, reasons, permission boundaries), never as Google coverage.
coverage.not_inspected_or_not_supplied: docs/storyboards.html (rendered), docs/checksums.sha256, toolchain-lock.json, README.md, gradlew/gradle-wrapper.jar, ui-svg/ and tooling/ sources, catalog/contracts/openapi.json and catalog/API-CONTRACT.md, the executable catalog and configuration DDL (bridge-config.sql), JSON Schemas, ARC upstream C# sources, the portable zip member list, receipt stdout/stderr (hashes only). Prior design013 ledger entries were not mapped one-to-one to the current findings; the ledger cites a superseded requirement numbering (its 11, 9 and 3 correspond to current 8, 10 and 2).
coverage.unexplained_limitations_retained_in_scor: Container-label propagation is inferred from identical strings, not from CLI behavior; the arc-protobuf-v1 identifier and the 0.8.0 absence rest on the inspected text and the proto, not on upstream C# sources; the HTML slideshow's self-containment could not be observed.

limitations: No tools, shell, network or device actions were used; SHA-256 values and byte offsets were taken as supplied and not recomputed; SVGs were read as XML text, not rendered.

Platform statements marked as reviewer recollection (FLAG_SECURE capture blanking, ACTION_USER_UNLOCKED receiver delivery, Ktor CIO server TLS, package visibility on API 30+, Wireless Debugging Wi-Fi prerequisite, screencap/input display-ID semantics, MCP 404/400 and -32002 wording, stable-AIDL meta transactions, Marp HTML image handling) are reported as uncertainty and carry verification_needed; none is asserted as fact and none alone drives a score.
Build receipts attest exit code and output count only; they are treated as claimed runs, not as proof of determinism.
Severities reflect impact on design correctness, implementability and requirement completeness only; implementation, dataset and Google inventory status were not scored.
Scores are a single holistic judgment of the whole design, not an average of workpaper severities, and no target score was applied.
